title: Digital Age ~ CLO6 Launch Event Replay [Continuously Updating] p05 Director Dai's Speech at Shanda University
description: Didn't have time to finish watching the live broadcast? No time to watch it live? No worries! The CLO6 launch event recording is here~ Come and take a look!
transcript:
Hello, everyone. I am a teacher from the Fashion and Fashion Design Department of Shanghai Shanda College.  
What is different from the guests just now is that I learned about the experience of marketing from the perspective of product design.  
I think it is more about how we can improve our experience, especially in the field of psychology, to express my thoughts on Clou.  
What I think represents Clou is that Clou is a place where we can learn from each other.  
Clou is a place where we can learn from each other.  
For example, there are many young designers and school teachers in China.  
I myself have developed some of the brand products for my own business, be it electronics, fashion or physical electronics.  
I have also done various virtual-related courses in our team.  
I have done a lot of virtual virtual classes.  
In 2012, when I was in Korea, I found out that Clou was so popular in China.  
I discovered such a software.  
At that time, communication was still done mostly through forums.  
The reason I found it actually comes from my own habit of doing research.  
When I was doing research, I found it ridiculous that we had to do fitting over and over again, making many modifications repeatedly.  
How could there be no such software?  
Then I searched and found that such software appeared in Korea.  
I started to learn bit by bit through the course tutorials.  
After I graduated, I entered academia.  
Then I continuously found that many peers around me started paying attention to this software.  
I think there are many epoch-making products in our era, like WeChat and Alibaba.  
I believe Clou, for our fashion design field, is an epoch-making product.  
Earlier, a guest asked how long it would take for Clou to completely replace our real-world process.  
I want to tell everyone that our team conducted a regional survey, including many designers, researchers, and educators in the industry.  
We believe the replacement period should be about five years.  
This data is based on our real survey results.  
Based on this data, not only our schools, such as Beijing Institute of Fashion Technology, Donghua University, and China Academy of Art, have all started offering courses like this.  
From an educator’s perspective, the education industry can sometimes be more sensitive because our talent training must anticipate what kind of market students will face four years later.  
We must formulate corresponding training programs accordingly.  
We believe that most teachers in the domestic education system have started to fully promote Clou’s software.  
This is not only for ourselves but also for actual market demand.  
So if anyone is worried about talent issues, you can contact me.  
We currently have many students working in different companies engaging in virtual design using Clou.  
On the other hand, when we carry out projects, at the very beginning of the project process, we create a lot of creative works.  
Here, I will show you some student assignments.  
For all our works now, we require students in the school to make virtual runway presentations.  
As you can see, for many creative works, we have already achieved quite a high degree of realism.  
Not only in fabric drape but also in the application of patterns.  
You can see from these just now, some of the styles are quite complex.  
This is because students’ graduation designs often use many...  

This is a basic judgment of Chinese educational talent in the market: in the past, our education was more inclined towards artistic education.  
In the 20th year of the reform and opening up, we began to try some brand education.  
We believe that in the next 10 years, education will be digitalized.  
Of course, this digitalization will not only remain in digital design itself but will also combine with VR and AR technologies.  
Last year, we started a crowdfunding project with a well-known partner brand, Liyingfang.  
So how to improve the experience?  
In fact, we will go through different modes.  
The first is cooperation with the brand Liyingfang.  
We will turn some student design styles into virtualized versions.  
Then they can choose.  
This is the first step.  
The second step is to put this virtualized image, especially on the same clothes.  
As you know, it is very difficult to complete the same clothes for children aged 3 to 5 years old because children find it hard to show off.  
At this time, Clou’s virtualization has a very good effect.  
We can present the details of the same clothes in the virtual show, including the virtual runway.  
The third is the key to the experience.  
Sometimes children may draw some works, and they want to put those works on clothes as patterns.  
This idea actually comes from some VIP customers of Liyingfang, and we help realize it.  
How to achieve it?  
Maybe this child values this style in the store, then we scan his artwork.  
Children can customize patterns on their own clothes.  
The third step is that we are now in the process where children wear VR glasses.  
They can experience the design they made in Clou, viewing details in this kind of display.  
This aspect not only promotes the overall brand image—  
The brand will become more technological.  
At the same time, it also contributes to understanding the consumption habits of real-time customers.  
I can show you what we are doing.  
You may see this is a uniform we are making, where children can put their own works.  
The image here is for correction and alternatives.  
It can enhance children’s own styles.  
As for the benefits of Clou, previous guests have already talked about it in detail, so I don’t think I need to go into detail.  
But what I want to say is that we are not only concerned with the software design itself but also with digital assets.  
There is a lot of international research ongoing, especially with the pandemic.  
Many of us have started online meetings.  
The latest project we are working on with some companies is a virtual avatar project.  
What does this mean?  
In the future, our clothes will not only serve as physical garments but also virtual clothes may be sold.  
For example, when you are in a meeting, your virtual avatar will become key in sales.  
I think by then, whether actively or passively, we must learn this software because we want to build such virtual avatars.  
They will become virtual assets.  
This is a small test of the project we are doing.  
We placed an image of Clou’s software in a test mirror so customers can see the large images they made through the test mirror, especially children.  
They may not see the image clearly on the computer but can see it in the test mirror.  
They can see some of the pictures they made on Clou’s clothes.  
The next step is linking with VR and AR.  
Now we are also beginning to connect with some small—no, not small—small design brands.  
I believe this model will be increasingly accepted by many companies.  
I can also introduce our own school here.  
Shanda College is the only school in the country registered with the Ministry of Education.  
The characteristic is that we are managed by the country, unlike other schools under the Ministry of Education.  
Secondly, we have a very rich and flexible mechanism, so we can work with many companies to develop some of these projects.  
In our project development, especially in digitalization, Clou is the foundation of all our projects.  
Whether we want to do this experience or VR in the future, we all need to use Clou’s software to design many styles.  
This is also what most of our courses have transformed into.  
It has been transformed into digital design.  
It may even be more important than our handmade production and handmade pattern making.  
This is my speech today.

chunks.title: Digital Age ~ CLO6 Launch Event Replay [Continuously Updating] p05 Director Dai's Speech at Shanda University
chunks.content: ## Introduction to Clou from a Product Design and Marketing Perspective This section covers insights into Clou software from the viewpoint of product design, marketing, and education, emphasizing its role in virtual fashion design and industry collaboration. It highlights Clou as a collaborative learning platform widely adopted by young designers, educators, and industry professionals. A teacher from the Fashion and Fashion Design Department of Shanghai Shanda College shared her unique perspective on Clou, focusing on improving user experience through psychological insights and product design. She emphasized that Clou is a platform for mutual learning, especially popular among young designers and educators in China. Having developed brand products across electronics and fashion, she discovered Clou during a 2012 visit to Korea, initially researching software solutions to avoid repetitive physical fittings in fashion design. At that time, communication about such tools was mostly through forums. Upon finding Clou software in Korea, she began learning it through tutorials, later entering academia and observing rising interest among peers. She compared Clou's impact on fashion design to epoch-making products like WeChat and Alibaba in their respective industries, underlining Clou’s transformative potential in digital fashion design. ## Adoption Timeline and Educational Integration of Clou This section details survey data on Clou adoption timelines, integration into educational curricula, and strategic talent training to meet future market needs, highlighting key fashion institutions adopting Clou. Responding to questions about how long Clou would take to replace traditional real-world fashion processes, she cited a regional survey involving designers, researchers, and educators estimating a five-year full adoption period. Multiple prominent institutions such as Beijing Institute of Fashion Technology, Donghua University, and China Academy of Art have incorporated Clou courses. From an educational perspective, training programs must anticipate market demands students will face four years post-graduation. Thus, many domestic educators actively promote Clou software to align talent development with industry needs. She also offered support for concerns about talent shortages, noting many students trained with Clou are already employed in virtual design roles across companies. ## Virtual Design Projects and Student Work Using Clou This section presents examples of student projects and educational practices involving Clou, demonstrating its capabilities in virtual runway presentations, fabric draping, and pattern application with high realism. At the project inception stage, students produce numerous creative works requiring virtual runway presentations. These presentations showcase advanced realism in fabric drape and complex pattern applications, reflecting the quality of graduation designs. This practice reflects a shift in Chinese education from purely artistic training toward integrating brand education and digital design, setting the stage for future educational digitalization combined with VR and AR technologies. ## Digital Transformation in Fashion Education and Brand Collaboration This section explains ongoing efforts in digitalizing fashion education and brand collaborations, particularly the partnership with Liyingfang, focusing on virtualizing student designs and enhancing children’s apparel customization through Clou. Since the 20th year of reform and opening up, Chinese education has evolved from art-focused toward brand and digital education.

chunks.title: Digital Age ~ CLO6 Launch Event Replay [Continuously Updating] p05 Director Dai's Speech at Shanda University
chunks.content: This practice reflects a shift in Chinese education from purely artistic training toward integrating brand education and digital design, setting the stage for future educational digitalization combined with VR and AR technologies. ## Digital Transformation in Fashion Education and Brand Collaboration This section explains ongoing efforts in digitalizing fashion education and brand collaborations, particularly the partnership with Liyingfang, focusing on virtualizing student designs and enhancing children’s apparel customization through Clou. Since the 20th year of reform and opening up, Chinese education has evolved from art-focused toward brand and digital education. Digitalization is expected to expand beyond design to include VR and AR integration. A crowdfunding project with partner brand Liyingfang aims to virtualize student design styles for consumer choice. Key applications include virtualizing children's clothing, which is challenging due to difficulties in fitting and presentation with young children aged 3 to 5. Clou’s virtualization allows detailed virtual runway displays of the same clothing, overcoming these challenges. Additionally, children can customize clothes with their own artwork scanned and applied as patterns, an idea inspired by VIP customers of Liyingfang. The next phase involves children wearing VR glasses to experience their Clou-designed clothes virtually, enhancing brand image through technology and enabling real-time consumer behavior insights. ## Use of Clou in Creating Digital Assets and Virtual Avatars This section discusses Clou’s role beyond software design, focusing on digital assets, virtual avatar creation, and future market trends for virtual clothing sales and avatar-based interactions. The team is engaged in international research, accelerated by the pandemic's shift to online meetings, working on virtual avatar projects. The vision is that clothing will exist as both physical and virtual assets, with virtual clothes sold and worn by avatars in virtual meetings and sales scenarios. The creation of virtual avatars requires mastering Clou software since these avatars represent valuable digital assets. A test project integrates Clou images into a "test mirror," allowing customers, especially children, to see large-scale versions of their designs that may not be clear on computer screens. This enhances engagement and visualization. Future developments include linking Clou outputs with VR and AR technologies and collaboration with emerging design brands, expecting broad industry acceptance. ## Institutional Context and Project Development at Shanghai Shanda College This section outlines Shanghai Shanda College’s unique institutional status, flexible mechanisms for industry collaboration, and its central role in digital and virtual fashion projects using Clou. Shanghai Shanda College is uniquely registered with the Ministry of Education and directly managed by the state, unlike other educational institutions. This status grants it a flexible operational model that facilitates partnerships with various companies. Clou forms the foundation of all digitalization projects at the college. Whether developing virtual experiences or VR applications, Clou is essential for designing styles. Most courses have transitioned from traditional handmade production and pattern making to digital design methods centered on Clou software, reflecting the college’s forward-looking educational approach.
